html:
SMTO-HTTP-0058 — These connection settings are too large to save

GUID: fbef05fa-eb69-4080-ad17-855bb5ad869e
Slug: http-profile-input-too-large
Domain: HTTP · Subsystem: http

What happened

  • The connection settings you tried to save are larger than SMTO's 1 MB limit, so nothing was saved. This usually means a lot of text, such as a whole web response, was pasted into a field.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the connection in Parameter Store and look for any field holding a lot of pasted text, such as a full web page or response, and remove it. Connection settings only need addresses, sign-in details and a few options, not large blocks of data.
  2. If you pasted a large certificate, choose File on Gateway under Custom certificate authority and enter the file's location instead. This keeps the certificate on the Gateway's computer instead of inside the saved settings.
  3. Select Save again. Once the settings are under the limit, SMTO accepts them.

What success looks like

  • The connection saves without an error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete other connections or saved data to make room; the limit applies to this one save, not to your overall storage.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The HTTP connection route read more than 1 MiB of request body and returned HTTP 413 before parsing it.

What this means

  • The connection editor read more than 1 MiB of request input and rejected it before JSON admission. The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The connection editor read more than 1 MiB of request input and rejected it before JSON admission.

How to diagnose it

  • Measure the submitted configuration payload, excluding any unrelated response data that should not be stored there.

How to fix it

  • Keep the body sent to the connection's save or test route under /api/agent/http/connections/ below 1 MiB: store only the supported profile fields, move large certificate bundles to a CA file path on the Gateway, and remove response bodies or unrelated data from the profile.
  • Reduce the configuration to the necessary supported fields and references. Do not place response payloads or unrelated data in connection configuration.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The supported edit stays within the 1 MiB input bound.

What not to do

  • Do not erase authoritative receipts or protected current input to conceal a size/capacity problem.

Technical notes

  • The specific receipt owns dispatch and effect truth. Authentication exchanges, resource requests and Gateway admission are separate phases; rendering this explanation performs no request and never authorizes replay of an uncertain mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
